newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran president urges Afghans to end civil war.
newsitem.headline: Iran president urges Afghans to end civil war.

text.p: Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani on Friday called on Afghan factions to stop fighting and set up a joint administration in the neighbouring country.

"I wish to God that they come to their senses, stop fighting and let one person, one group, one party or an joint assembly make peace in the country," Rafsanjani said in a mass prayer sermon broadcast on Tehran radio.

"Unfortunately, the Afghan groups do not stop fighting no matter how many times we advise them that the military option is not the proper way to solve problems," Rafsanjani told the crowd of worshippers gathered at Tehran University.
He did not address the capture of Kabul by the Taleban Islamic militia and did not name any of the Afghan groups.
"If this continues, we shall witness more misery and displacement for the Afghan people for years to come," Rafsanjani added.
The Taleban appeared in full control of Kabul on Friday after capturing the capital overnight. Government forces withdrew hours before the militia entered the city.
Iran has supported the Kabul government as legitimate. It has been hostile to the Taleban, whom Iranian media accused of being manipulated by Pakistan and the United States.
But Iran's media appeared to have toned down their criticism of the Taleban in the past few weeks and Iranian officials have held talks with representatives of the militia.
